messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.33-7
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.33-7) has been released at its web site
(http://www.rqtl.org) and will soon appear on CRAN.

Major changes:

  Can read/write 4-way cross data in MapQTL format (thanks to Timothee
  Flutre).

Minor changes:

  read.cross with format="qtlcart" can now read doubled haploids
  (dh/Ri0).

  Fixed potential problem in read.cross with format="csv" or "csvs" when
  there are many empty cells in the phenotype data.

  Fixed bug in read.cross for format="csv" that shows up in some rare
  cases: markers not ordered by linkage group, no positions provided,
  and chromosome IDs non-numeric. It was a pretty bad bug, as marker
  genotypes got scrambled.

  Fixed some memory leaks in MQM code.

Karl Broman

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] how can plot qtls on linkage map
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] how can plot qtls on linkage map
messages.body_plain:
If you just want to add dots (perhaps with different colors) to the genetic map, I'd just call points().
In the plot from plot.map, the x-axis locations of the chromosomes are 1, 2, ..., n_chr.

Here's an example using the hyper data.

data(hyper)
out <- scanone(calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1))
qtl <- summary(out, threshold=3)

plotMap(hyper, shift=FALSE) # shift=FALSE to _not_ move starting marker to 0 cM
for(i in 1:nrow(qtl)) {
  whchr <- match(qtl[i,1], chrnames(hyper))
  points(whchr+0.4, qtl[i,2], pch=21, bg="slateblue")
}

karl

messages.subject: Re: saving map
messages.body_plain:
One way is to use replace.map to add it to your cross and then pull.map with as.table=TRUE to make a tabular version of the map. Then write.csv to write to a comma-delimited file.

  mycross <- replace.map(mycross, mymap)
  mymapAsTable <- pull.map(mymap, as.table=TRUE)
  write.csv(mymapAsTable, file="mymap.csv")

karl

messages.subject: Re: question about plotLodProfile
messages.body_plain:
On Monday, August 18, 2014 12:11:57 PM UTC-5, can wrote:
> I am using the R/QTL for my research.
>
> One problem I am facing is that when I using the plotLodProfile function, it can only give me the plot on the chromosome(s) that QTL identified. How can I include all the chromosomes in the plot (including those no QTL was identified)?
>

You can use the argument showallchr=TRUE.  Here's an example.

  data(fake.bc)
  fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=1)
  qtl <- makeqtl(fake.bc, chr=c(2,5), pos=c(32.5, 17.5),
                 what="prob")
  rqtl <- refineqtl(fake.bc, qtl=qtl, method="hk",
                    keeplodprofile=TRUE)
  plotLodProfile(rqtl, showallchr=TRUE)

>
> Also, is it possbile to add the LOD threshold line to the above plot?

Use something like abline(h=3.5)

karl

messages.subject: dropped covariates
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

I try to perform a single QTL scan in F2 intercross (119 F2 hybrids; 140 markers genotyped, of them 3 markers are on chromosome X). Though the phenotype distribution is not normal, I try to explore my data in a normal model (and further to interpret results with caution). I do not get any warnings or errors in a scan without covariates. But when I try to include ‘sex’ covariate in the analyses, I receive warnings that I do not understand fully. Could you, please, tell why do I receive these warnings? Can I avoid them somehow?

Thank you.

> as <- F2NC$pheno[,c("sex")]

> is <- F2NC$pheno[,c("sex")]

> F2NC.resultaddsex <- scanone(F2NC, pheno.col=2, method="em", model="normal", addcovar=as, n.perm=0)

Warning message:

In scanone(F2NC, pheno.col = 2, method = "em", model = "normal",  :

  Dropped 1 additive covariates on X chromosome.

> F2NC.resultintsex <- scanone(F2NC, pheno.col=2, method="em", model="normal", addcovar=as, intcovar=is, n.perm=0)

Warning messages:

1: In scanone(F2NC, pheno.col = 2, method = "em", model = "normal",  :

  Dropped 1 additive covariates on X chromosome.

2: In scanone(F2NC, pheno.col = 2, method = "em", model = "normal",  :

  Dropped 1 interactive covariates on X chromosome.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am running a QTL analysis with 20 different wheat phenotypes and would want to plot the LOD profiles of all simultaneously.

Below is the code I'm using for the plots, z is the summary of the scaneone (with 1000 permutations). As a next step I want to make a pdf file with one plot for each phenotype, so 20 plots in one file.

z<-summary(cross.sc1.perms, alpha=.05)
pdf(file="12_QTL Plots.pdf", width=11, height=8.5)
for(i in 2:nphe(cross)){
  plot(cross.sc1, lodcolumn=i, lwd=1.5, gap=0, bandcol="gray70", incl.markers=TRUE, ylab="LOD", main=colnames(cross$pheno[i]), xlab=c("Threshold for alpha=.05 using 1000 permutations", z[i]))
  add.threshold(cross.sc1, perms=cross.sc1.perms, alpha=0.05, lodcolumn=i, gap=0)
}

I keep gettingError in plot.scanone(qtl.sc1, lodcolumn = i, lwd = 1.5, gap = 0, bandcol = "gray70", :
  Argument lodcolumn misspecified.
Can I not define lodcolumn this way?

Thanks,
Sandra

messages.body_plain:
It should work just as you've done it, but the error "Argument lodcolumn misspecified" indicates that you're pointing to a column that doesn't exist.

Try

  ncol(cross.sc1)

to see how many columns there are in cross.sc1. If there are 8 columns (which includes the columns for chromosome and position) than lodcolumn would need to be between 1 and 6.

karl

messages.subject: checkAlleles alternative for 4way design
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am working with a 4way mapping population of 400 individuals genotyped at ~1200 SNP loci. I used Stacks to call genotypes, estimated my original map using JoinMap, and have now loaded all my geno and phenotype data into R/qtl. I am performing the initial data diagnostics such as checking for segregation distortion and counting crossovers etc. but have found that 'checkAlleles' does not work for a 4way design. I can use 'calc.errorlod' to get a list of genotypes that are potentially wrong but I am having trouble coming up with a threshold for which markers to keep or discard, and when to throw out the whole marker vs. the specific datapoint. When I re-estimated my map in rqtl several chromosomes were inflated to 6000cM. I believe this strongly suggests I have some mis-called genotypes or markers out of order.

Is there a rigorous way to come up with a threshold or should I get rid of everything with a LOD >4.0?
Are there any other functions that do not work for a 4way design?

Thanks,
Liz

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] checkAlleles alternative for 4way design
messages.body_plain:
checkAlleles serves a somewhat different purpose from calc.errorlod.  checkAlleles is looking for cases where the parental alleles should be switched (a marker's genotypes are strongly associated with genotypes at other markers, but with recombination fractions near 1 rather than near 0). The error LOD scores are looking for tight double-crossovers indicative of genotyping errors. The error LOD scores might show the former, but probably the genetic map will be distorted which could make the error LOD scores less informative.

You could do a plot of the LOD scores vs rec. fracs. from est.rf, and look for cases where LOD is large and rf is >> 0.5.

  data(fake.4way)
  fake.4way <- est.rf(fake.4way)
  rf <- pull.rf(fake.4way)
  lod <- pull.rf(fake.4way, "lod")
  plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod))

I think there are a number of other functions that don't work for the 4-way design, but unfortunately I don't have a list of which ones they are.

karl
